## What is a time series foundation model?

* Large, pre-trained models (e.g. Chronos, TimeGPT, Moirai) that forecast directly from
  historical data
* Trained once on huge, diverse collections of time series
* Little or no task-specific training required to forecast a new series ("zero-shot")

## How do they compare to classical methods?

* Classical methods (ETS, ARIMA, regression) are fit to *your* series
* Foundation models are pre-trained on *many* series, then applied to yours
* Trade-offs: convenience and speed vs. interpretability and control

## When to use a foundation model

* Useful for quick baselines, and series with little historical data
* Classical methods often still competitive, and more transparent, once tuned
* Consider the operational context (compute, explainability, cost)

## Summary

* Foundation models are a fast-moving area of forecasting research
* A useful addition to the toolkit alongside ETS, ARIMA and regression
* This session gives a high-level introduction; hands-on examples to follow
